title: Does the best rotor cant angle change when yaw reaction torque scales with propeller size?
lede: does the interior cant optimum survive a reaction torque that grows with propeller diameter (κ = c·D) instead of a fixed 0.016 m? In simulation yes: for c = 0.06, 0.126 and 0.25 the joint co-design reaches 12.5°, 12.3° and 11.8° held-out attitude error with the bound at 80°, picks 33–41° each time, and cant still beats no cant in 5 of 5 seeds; the gain is largest (−4.8°) for the weakest reaction torque.
summary: Follow-up to codesign-aero-cant-bound, where the yaw reaction torque per newton of thrust κ was a fixed 0.016 m whatever the propeller. For a propeller Q/T = (CP/CT) D/(2π), so here κ = c D with c swept over 0.06, 0.126 and 0.25 (CP/CT about 0.38, 0.79, 1.6; 0.126 reproduces 0.016 m at 127 mm). Joint CMA-ES over arm length, propeller size, cant and six PID gains (1920 evaluations, 5 seeds, 64 held-out episodes), cant bound 0, 35° or 80°. At bound 80° the held-out error is 12.54°, 12.28° and 11.84° for c = 0.06, 0.126, 0.25 (fixed κ: 12.30°); with no cant it is 17.30°, 16.26°, 14.13° (fixed: 15.18°), so cant helps by 4.8°, 4.0° and 2.3°, better in 5 of 5 paired seeds each. The chosen cant is 33–41° at bound 80°, and the 35° bound loses at most 0.03° against it. Limits: c is swept, not taken from propeller data (the UIUC propeller database host was unreachable from the run sandbox); cost, mass and plant ranges are inherited assumed fits; attitude steps only, no hardware.
